entities.summary: Filippo Calandrini was a half-brother of Pope Nicholas V and a prominent Italian Roman Catholic cardinal in the 15th century. Born in unknown circumstances, he rose to prominence as a papal legate in the 1450s, playing a key role in the Sienese Wars and the Pazzi conspiracy against the Medici. Calandrini's influence extended to the Vatican, where he contributed to the reform efforts of Pope Nicholas V, who later succeeded him as Pope. As a cardinal, Calandrini participated in the conclave that elected Pope Nicholas V, shaping the course of the Catholic Church during the Renaissance. His legacy as a papal legate and cardinal continues to be studied by historians today. The Italian city of Siena, where Calandrini played a crucial role in the Sienese Wars, remains a testament to his enduring impact on the region's history.
